pending.kill_criteria: (1) T1 drop fall collection day dac truoc khi GritFell co creative san -> doi sang Christmas window; (2) DECOY/Duck Camp tung species-art dove truoc -> mat differentiation, xet lai
pending.evidence: Drake homepage escalation 24/07 + clearance wave 3/9 brand + DECOY van 1 SKU + 25/07: SITKA fall drop (fall pivot lan toi T3, cua so hep dan) + F&T Gulfstream $108 validate lane field-to-town (species-art gap van trong) + 26/07: TX South Zone opener moved to 1/9 (all TX zones now open Sept 1 -> national simultaneous opener) + Etsy dove market = 100% slogan tees $12-25 (species-art gap confirmed demand-side) + 27/07: TPWD news release opened LIVE (PRIMARY) confirms all-TX Sept 1 opener + white-winged days eliminated; Mon sweep: NO brand of 11 running public dove creative (Huk pivoted to back-to-school, Drake EST holds); FF x Trout Unlimited limited-500 validates species-art scarcity at $74+ (GritFell <$60 gap open). Score held 4/5. + 28/07: FF x TU limited-500 SOLD OUT ('Only 0 left', 2nd annual; year 1 sold out in 24h per Free Fly) = species-art scarcity proven to convert; F&S hunting index has ZERO dove content (media silence too); Poncho went gameday-licensed not dove. Score held 4/5, 10 days to kill_date. + 29/07 RE-SCORE 4/5 -> 3/5: (a) Duck Camp launched 'Game Series' = 32 species-embroidery hats at $36 (Fall '26) -> the 'nobody plays species-art in the accessible accessory tier' premise is DEAD (logged in metrics.rejected); kill criterion (2) NOT triggered because Duck Camp has NO dove/teal SKU; (b) Meta Ad Library (first live run) shows Hunthide running 9 ACTIVE dove ads since 23/07 incl gift-framed 'The gift he'll actually wear' (28/07) -> paid dove channel is no longer empty, though 0/11 rotation brands and editorial remain silent. Window still open on POSITIONING (moment-specific subject + gift frame + no-discount), no longer open on SURPRISE. 9 days to kill_date. + 30/07 SHAPE CHANGE, score held 3/5 but the two halves moved in opposite directions. (a) DOVE HALF WEAKER: Meta Ad Library shows the dove paid lane went 1 -> >=4 apparel advertisers in 24h (Cordia 2 ads created 29/07 incl 'Dove Season Is Almost Here' + 'Free Shipping and Returns'; Dove Gear 'The Last Bird Vest You'll Ever Need'; Rack and Wing Co. 'Dove Field Pocket Tee'; Hunthide still active) — none in the 11 rotation, all cheap/POD tier. Arbitrage T lowered T3 -> T2. GritFell has NO dove art or SKU, so entering now means entering last and empty-handed. (b) TEAL HALF STRONGER: 'teal season' query returns ZERO hunting-apparel advertisers, same season window; and the 30/07 self-audit of /collections/hat found GritFell ALREADY OWNS 'Early Teal' ($34) plus 'Pheasant Opener' ($34) — the long-carried 'no teal SKU' claim is FALSIFIED. So the teal side needs no new blank, only art review + copy + creative. (c) Context: 0/11 rotation brands run any opener creative 33 days out (Drake is on 'Past Season Sale', Free Fly on 'End of Summer'). BOT RECOMMENDATION: if approved, approve TEAL-FIRST and drop or defer the dove half. 8 days to kill_date. + 31/07 TEAL HALF STRENGTHENS AGAIN, score held 3/5. (a) 'teal season' on Meta Ad Library (US, ACTIVE) returns ZERO hunting-apparel advertisers for the SECOND consecutive day, while the dove lane counted >=4 on 30/07. (b) First COMPLETE 90-SKU sweep of gritfell.com/collections/all confirms the asset position precisely: 'Early Teal' exists as a HAT ($34) but there is NO teal design on any shirt/polo/swim blank — so a teal-first approval can ship the hat immediately while apparel needs a design translation, not a new idea. Same sweep shows 0/90 SKUs carry sale pricing. (c) Radar context corrected: 0/11 rotation brands run opener-countdown creative, but Tom Beckbe now leads its homepage with 'Tom Beckbe x Ducks Unlimited' ($495 DU Fowler Vest, $375 DU Double Timber Bag) — the conservation-partnership language a species-art brand might otherwise reach for is being taken at the premium tier. (d) Howler and Tom Beckbe both discount ZERO, confirming the no-discount posture is normal above the mid tier. 7 days to kill_date. + 01/08 SCORE HELD 3/5, halves keep diverging. (a) DOVE HALF WEAKER AGAIN: the lane escalated OUT of the cheap POD tier — Ball and Buck, a heritage US hunting-apparel brand, created 'Dove Season Essentials from Ball and Bck' on 31/07, and Hunthide refreshed its whole creative set the same day. GritFell would now be entering behind both a POD wave and a heritage brand, still with no dove art. (b) TEAL HALF HOLDS: 'teal season' returns ZERO hunting-apparel advertisers for the THIRD straight day (30/07, 31/07, 01/08); one unresolved outdoors-named page with an untitled creative is counted on neither side. (c) NEW BLOCKER FOUND ON OUR SIDE: the /products/early-teal page opens, but its description says nothing whatsoever about the bird — it is pure blank spec ('Classic 5-panel baseball cap', 'Engineered for comfort. Built for the wild.'). So if teal-first is approved, the first task is NOT ads, it is rewriting the listing; and the standing question 'is the art a moment or a static portrait' still needs a human to open the image. (d) TIER CONTEXT WORSENED: DECOY came back online after a 7-day block and turns out to run 33 species-embroidery hats at $34.99 (no dove, no teal) — so the accessible species-art hat tier now holds FOUR brands at $34-36, two of which discount. (e) Coincidence worth using: 07/08 is both this item's kill_date and the USFWS Prairie Pothole comment deadline. 6 days to kill_date.

pending.title: Numbered Species Drop — capsule species-art phat hanh danh so, so luong chot, zero discount (mechanics hoc tu Free Fly x Trout Unlimited)
pending.kill_criteria: (1) OPENER-CAPSULE-2026 bi reject -> mat vehicle gan nhat, xet lai; (2) xuat hien case limited-drop e/khong ban het o tier accessible (<$60) cho thay mechanics khong dich xuong duoi premium
pending.evidence: 27/07: FF x TU hoodie 'ONLY 500 AVAILABLE' featured homepage (species art + conservation + numbered scarcity, $98). 28/07: product page live = SOLD OUT ('Out of Stock $98', 'Only 0 left'); page states year-1 drop sold out in 24h; 2nd annual 2026 edition -> annual-franchise mechanics (restock-as-news + scarcity). Chua co case nao o tier <$60 — do la cau hoi mo. + 29/07: Duck Camp Game Series is an ALWAYS-ON program (not numbered, not capped) and 14/32 SKUs already discounted to $25 — so it is not a counter-example to limited/numbered mechanics at the sub-$60 tier. Score held 3/5. + 30/07: no new evidence for or against. Adjacent finding worth noting for whoever decides — GritFell already has 36 species-embroidery hats at one price with NO program name and NO season tag, while Duck Camp bundles 32 into 'Game Series / New for Fall 26'. A named program is the cheapest version of this mechanic and needs no price or scarcity change. Score held 3/5, 22 days to kill_date. + 31/07: mild support, score held 3/5. Complete 90-SKU sweep shows 0/90 GritFell SKUs have ever carried sale pricing — the no-discount discipline a numbered/limited drop depends on is already the brand's actual operating posture, so the mechanic would not require a behaviour change. Independently, both T6 rotation brands (Howler $75-145, Tom Beckbe $195-495) also run zero discounts, i.e. no-discount is the norm above the mid tier rather than an eccentric stance. Still NO observed case of numbered/limited mechanics at the sub-$60 tier — that remains the open question. 21 days to kill_date. + 01/08: the open question finally has a data point, and it cuts against the premise. DECOY (unblocked today after 7 days) discounts a $34.99 Corduroy Rope Hat to $17.49 — a ~50% cut inside GritFell's own hat tier. Together with Duck Camp (14 of 32 Game Series hats at $25), there are now TWO independent precedents for deep discounting at the sub-$60 accessible tier. Reading: numbered/limited scarcity mechanics have still never been OBSERVED at this tier, and the tier's actual norm is discounting, not scarcity. That does not kill the idea — it reframes it: GritFell's 0/90-never-discounted posture is a deliberate difference rather than the tier standard, so a numbered drop would be a way of SAYING that difference out loud. Caveat found the same day: the brand's no-discount posture is real on unit price but NOT on offer, since the site runs 'BUY 2 GET 1 FREE' in the banner and a conflicting 'BUY 2, SAVE 15%' on product pages. Score held 3/5, 20 days to kill_date.
